# Appeal of Denial — Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT 23472)

**RE:** Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18
**Member:** Reese Carter
**Member ID:** W451155739
**Plan:** Iowa Total Care (Commercial/ACA), State of Iowa
**Reference Number:** POC-EF30A43966-84895
**Governing Policy Named in This Appeal:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines (https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf), effective 2026-07-01

Dear Iowa Total Care Appeals Department,

I am writing to request a reconsideration of the denial of my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I do not believe the denial reflects the full record of the conservative treatment I have already completed.

**A note on the criteria cited.** The denial states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. However, the policy language I have been able to review — provided to me for this appeal — is drawn from the cervical spine fusion sections of the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines (criteria addressing ACDF, cervical posterior decompression with fusion, and axial neck pain). Those sections govern neck surgery, not shoulder replacement, and I do not believe they are the correct criteria against which my request should have been measured. I am not quoting them here as if they apply to my case, because they do not appear to. I am asking the plan to identify and provide, in writing, the specific shoulder replacement / conservative-care criteria it actually applied to my request.

**Formal request for the applicable criteria.** Because Iowa Total Care routes musculoskeletal surgery review to Evolent, and Evolent's clinical criteria are published on RadMD, I am requesting that the plan confirm whether my request was reviewed under the Evolent Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines' shoulder replacement section, and provide me with the exact text of the criteria used to deny this request. I am entitled to know the specific standard my case was measured against so that I can respond to it directly.

**The conservative treatment I have completed.** Regardless of which specific criteria apply, the record shows the following, which I ask the plan to weigh in its review:

- I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, from 2026-04-13 to 2026-07-20) focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-27, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my shoulder on 2026-07-07 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- I currently cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and my exam showed positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion.

This is a substantial and recent course of conservative treatment — physical therapy, medication, and injection — that did not resolve my symptoms, alongside imaging that documents a significant structural injury. I ask that the plan review this history against whatever conservative-care standard it actually applied, and provide that standard to me in writing as part of this appeal.

**Deadline and submission.** I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14. I am submitting it through the address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I may also submit it through ambetterhealth.com (selecting Iowa and the appeal/grievance form) or by calling the number on my member ID card.

I am requesting that Iowa Total Care reverse the denial of CPT 23472, or, at minimum, provide the specific criteria applied to my case so that I may respond to them fully.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Reese Carter
Member ID: W451155739
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note; MRI report dated 2026-07-07; injection record dated 2026-05-27; surgeon's documentation of medical necessity (Dr. Marchetti)

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
